headline: High: gpt-researcher can egress and ingest files, while spring-integration-samples is a non-runnable docs-only target with no documented isolation or verification, creating default-path leakage and cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, run browsers, and use MCP/OpenAI/Tavily APIs; if spring-integration-samples content is bridged into its research inputs, prompt-like content could steer outputs. The pair has no documented shared channel, but the interaction is plausible through files or copied artifacts, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is copied into gpt-researcher prompts or files
IF an MCP or filesystem bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Disable any shared workspace or copy-paste bridge
Restrict gpt-researcher to trusted input folders
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to imported content
Review MCP endpoints before enabling them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles secrets and has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples is non-runnable and has no data surfaces documented. If both are placed in a shared workspace, gpt-researcher could read and transmit sensitive local documents or API-backed research artifacts; uncertainty about the bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or mounted workspace
IF gpt-researcher is pointed at folders containing secrets or local documents
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Run gpt-researcher with a least-privilege API key
Audit outbound destinations before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can write indirectly via subprocesses and read files, but spring-integration-samples is marked runnable false and exposes no write or network capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, direct capability conflict is limited and best classified low.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is actually deployed as a writable service despite being marked non-runnable
IF both agents are given the same mutable directory or git checkout
mitigations: Keep the sample repo read-only
Do not mount the same output directory into both agents
Run only one writer per workspace
Use separate git branches for generated artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can generate research outputs, and spring-integration-samples could consume those outputs if an operator wires them together. Because no verification step is documented between them, the pair can propagate errors from generated research into downstream actions, though the action authority is not explicit.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples consumes gpt-researcher output as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between generation and use
mitigations: Add a manual review step before reuse
Require source citations on all generated claims
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and diff successive runs
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and may send them to third-party APIs; spring-integration-samples has no documented data classes or residency controls. The main compliance issue is a potential mismatch if regulated data is routed through gpt-researcher, but the second agent is not itself a documented data processor, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF outputs are retained or forwarded outside the operator's approved jurisdiction
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from prompts and files
Confirm API processing terms before use
Set short retention on generated reports
Store outputs in the approved region only
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
